bug_semantics: In setuid mode, singularity.conf 'limit container paths' is enforced by Image.AuthorizedPath on the container image path. Through SingularityCE 4.4.1 the check was strings.HasPrefix(i.Path, filepath.EvalSymlinks(filepath.Clean(limit))). That is a string-prefix test, not a directory-tree test, so a limit of /data/safe also authorizes sibling paths such as /data/safe-but-unsafe and /tmp/foo vs /tmp/foobar. filepath.Clean strips a trailing slash, so administrators cannot close the hole by writing /data/safe/. A low-privileged user who can place an image in a similarly named sibling directory bypasses the admin allowlist. The 4.4.2 fix compares filepath.Rel(limit, image) and accepts only '.' or filepath.IsLocal(rel).
flaw_origin: AuthorizedPath was added in 8ac2f4a613a30a3b7d4be55b2b1ab49fcd95ff00 (2018-06-24) as an exact match of filepath.Dir(i.Path) against each limit path; that helper was already called with LimitContainerPaths at the BIC parent. The sibling-prefix bug was first written in 48b4735d5a8d152af30123d6621b123ca87f9864 (2018-08-31, Cedric Clerget), which switched dirname from filepath.Dir(i.Path) to i.Path and replaced equality with strings.HasPrefix. Later 8d47ee667fca6bae3d5d7bde4806f8f502a8cbf3 only moved the file (internal/pkg/image -> pkg/image, 0-line change) and 608fcea15cbb6079dae7bd2865f2b865a03af738 only wrapped the same HasPrefix body with initFile(); neither is a first-write.
